newsitem.title: GERMANY: Czech CSA plans to expand ex-Germany air cargo.
newsitem.headline: Czech CSA plans to expand ex-Germany air cargo.

text.p: Czech airline CSA said it aims to increase air cargo sales revenue in Germany by 20 percent to more than one million marks this year.
Dusan Pavlasek, CSA passenger and cargo sales manager Germany, said cargo sales revenue rose five percent to 850,000 marks in 1996.
"In 1997 we want to earn more than one million marks in Germany turnover," he told Reuters in an interview.
CSA carried 670 tonnes of air cargo from Germany in 1996, including about one-third trucked to Prague by air cargo road feeder services, he added.
The Far East and the Middle East are the main destinations for CSA's Germany cargo with 25 percent share of volume.
"If we had more capacity than our twice-weekly Bangkok and Singapore flights we could sell it," Pavlasek said.
The airline carried relatively little air cargo destined for the Czech and Slovak Republics due to tough competition from low-priced road transport from Germany, he noted.
CSA took over its own Germany air cargo sales in January 1996 from the previous GSA, Transnautic Aero GmbH, and appointed a dedicated cargo sales representative last June, Pavlasek said.
"The higher sales show that it was the right decision to part from Transnautic," he added. - Reuters Air Cargo Newsroom. Tel +44 171 542 7706 Fax +5017
